$comment: Generated by scripts/build-sample-pack.mjs. The recordings are not in this repository: `pnpm bench fetch` downloads each file from its pinned upstream commit, checks it against the sha256 below, and stores it (a WAV as FLAC-coded samples plus the `stored` head and tail bytes, which rebuild the published file exactly). `bytes` and `sha256` are always the published file; `storedBytes` is what the maintainer's flac produced and varies a little with the flac version.
description: Raw, permissively licensed recordings for Stagebench protocol 3: one grand, one upright, four electric pianos (one tine, two reed, one electric grand), and a pipe organ. Every file is byte-identical to what its author published; nothing is trimmed, levelled, re-encoded, or mapped by the pack.

sources.name: Salamander Grand Piano V3
sources.author: Alexander Holm
sources.attribution: Salamander Grand Piano V3 by Alexander Holm, licensed under CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Source: https://archive.org/details/SalamanderGrandPianoV3
sources.format: FLAC, 48 kHz, 24-bit, stereo (two AKG C414 in AB, about 12 cm above the strings)
sources.selection: Eight of the sixteen velocity layers (v1, v2, v3, v4, v7, v10, v13, v16) for all 30 sampled notes (minor thirds, A0 to C8), plus every auxiliary recording: 88 hammer-release noises (rel*), 69 string-resonance recordings (harm*), and 4 pedal noises. v2 and v3 were added to the first six because the step from v1 to v4 (about 9 dB) was three times any other step between the kept layers; with them the largest step is under 5 dB. The other eight layers are left out to keep the pack a reasonable size; nothing that is included is altered.

sources.name: Upright Piano KW
sources.instrument: Kawai upright piano, recorded in a living room
sources.author: Gonzalo and Roberto (FreePats project)
sources.attribution: Upright Piano KW by Gonzalo and Roberto, FreePats project, CC0 1.0 (public domain dedication). Source: https://freepats.zenvoid.org/Piano/acoustic-grand-piano.html
sources.format: FLAC, 44.1 kHz, 24-bit, stereo (Zoom H1 at the player position)
sources.selection: The whole published sample set: 66 recordings in two dynamics (vL, vH), with the upstream README, LICENSE, and SFZ mapping.

sources.name: Greg Sullivan's E-Pianos

sources.author: Greg Sullivan

sources.name: Rhodes Mark I, GM version (Discord SFZ GM Bank)
sources.instrument: 1977 Rhodes Mark I Stage 73 (tine electric piano), recorded from the harp output
sources.author: Jeff Learman
licenseEvidence: Discord GM/Melodic/005-Electric Piano 1.sfz, header committed by the author (GitHub jlearman, commits 05d5ed8befa0 and 945cca9cab6e): "Author: Jeff Learman ... License: Creative Commons CC0, Jeff Learman ... Mapped and relooped for GM by jlearman"
The bank README: each instrument is licensed by its creator, with the terms in its .sfz file; only CC0, CC-BY, and equivalent licenses are allowed.
The author, on KVR (2022-11-14, https://www.kvraudio.com/forum/viewtopic.php?p=8555554#p8555554): "The Rhodes and acoustic guitar are CC0 for sure because I released them"
sources.attribution: Rhodes Mark I samples (jRhodes GM version) by Jeff Learman, CC0 1.0 (public domain dedication). Source: https://github.com/sfzinstruments/Discord-SFZ-GM-Bank
sources.format: WAV, 44.1 kHz, 16-bit, mono; shortened and looped by the author (loop points in each file’s smpl chunk)
sources.selection: The whole instrument as its author published it in the bank (General MIDI program 5, Electric Piano 1): 15 recordings, one dynamic per note, a root every three to six semitones from F1 to C7 (file names give the MIDI note), with its SFZ mappings and the bank README. The other instruments in the bank are not included.

sources.name: VCSL Pipe Organ
sources.instrument: Pipe organ, two registrations on the third manual
sources.author: Simon Dalzell (Ivy Audio), for Versilian Studios
sources.attribution: Pipe organ samples by Simon Dalzell (Ivy Audio), from the Versilian Community Sample Library by Versilian Studios LLC, CC0 1.0 (public domain dedication). Source: https://github.com/sgossner/VCSL
sources.format: WAV, 44.1 kHz, 16-bit, stereo, about 12 s per note
sources.selection: The two manual registrations, Loud (Rode_Man3Open_*) and Quiet (NT5_Man3Quiet_*), each with 21 notes in minor thirds from C1 to C6, plus the set’s Info.txt and the library README and LICENSE. The two pedal registrations (22 recordings) and the blower noise are left out for size, as is the rest of the library.
